crime_highlights: the appellant repeatedly sexually assaulted the complainant
the appellant chased her, threw her up against the wall, and then dragged her back to his bedroom
The appellant also threatened the complainant, saying that he was going to kill her and dump her body in a lake.
He took her cellphone, so that she could not call for help.
The appellant forced the complainant to make a recording saying that she had consented to the sexual activity.
the assault left her “terrified” to work in her chosen field, filled her with a sense of hopelessness
rationale_highlights: some of which arose from systemic considerations that shaped the life of the appellant as an Indigenous person

As an Aboriginal offender with significant challenges resulting in part from his early childhood years in such an impoverished and abusive environment (the legacy of intergenerational trauma), his level of moral culpability is reduced from what it would otherwise be.
I would therefore not accede to the request of Crown counsel to impose a sentence of 10 years, at the high end of the range.
note: Trial judge's reasons quoted by SCC; Gladue report not described in detail.

crime_highlights: Mr. Cope assaulted his common law partner.
He repeatedly threw her to the ground, kicked her in the head and ribs, and punched her in the face.
He also repeatedly smashed her face into a sidewalk and kicked her in the head as she lay motionless on the ground.
Mr. Cope’s prolonged and brutal assault was captured by a nearby surveillance video
She suffered severe injuries to her face, eyes, and body, requiring extensive medical treatment and plastic surgery.
rationale_highlights: The Court of Appeal then undertook a nuanced assessment of the moral blameworthiness of the respondent.
which in an Indigenous individual must be viewed through the lens of colonization and intergenerational trauma
The respondent’s connection to his language and cultural practices were directly severed by his family’s history with the Shubenacadie Residential School
These factors attenuate his moral blameworthiness

the fact that the respondent lives with a significant mental illness and was, as I described above, in a profoundly dysregulated state at the time of the aggravated assault attenuates his moral blameworthiness
note: Majority reasons; crime paragraphs taken from the dissent's facts (183-184).
